keyFindings.text: **BUG — P2: The worktree naming script lost its executable bit.** Commit `957f47570f381cfc42c2d90d151771dfe695647e` changed its Git mode from 100755 to 100644; `git ls-files -s` shows 100644 and `test -x` is false. The script has a Bash shebang at `.skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/worktree-naming.sh:1`, while the scripts README calls this the executable core at `.skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/README.md:17` and the skill directs allocation through that script path at `.skilled/skills/sk-git/SKILL.md:146`. A direct execution of the script path now fails; the explicit `bash .../worktree-naming.sh` examples remain usable. The related upgrade instruction is `.skilled/changelog/skilled/v4.2.0.0.md:915`. I could not confirm how often users execute the shorthand directly, so the impact is limited to direct invocation.

keyFindings.text: **DRIFT — P2: The Bladebro upgrade command bypasses the current verified install procedure.** Release-note line 906 directs users to run `npm install -g bladebro@4.8.2` (introduced by commit `c7f38f295d282f34efc292a7bc611c2019fb489e`). The current Bladebro install guide instead specifies `npm install -g --ignore-scripts bladebro@4.8.2` and a digest check before the installed binary first runs at `.skilled/skills/mcp-browser-use/mcp-bladebro/mcp-servers/bladebro-cli/README.md:24-27,50-58`; its wrapper enforces lifecycle scripts off and checks the launcher and native binary digests at `.skilled/skills/mcp-browser-use/mcp-bladebro/scripts/install.sh:147-173`. Commit `ec3ed74ad01edad7311aadfe7a117d4010b10919` added this installer posture. The release-note command omits both script suppression and verification, so it contradicts the current install contract. This confirms a lower-assurance command is published; it does not establish that the pinned package contains a malicious payload.
